intended_object: The canonical generators x_0, …, x_{n-1} of the pro-p group ⟨x_0,…,x_{n-1} | R⟩ presented on Fin n, i.e. the images of the free generators under the quotient map F_p(n) → F_p(n)/⟨⟨R⟩⟩. They are indexed by ℕ, with value 1 for indices outside the range. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body applies the quotient map `presentedProP.mk p rels` to `freeProPGen p n i`. `freeProPGen p n i` is `freeProP.of ⟨i, h⟩` when i < n and 1 otherwise. So for i < n the value is the image of the i-th free generator, which is the i-th canonical generator of the presented group (`presentedProPGen_of_lt`). For i ≥ n the value is 1 (`presentedProPGen_eq_one_of_le`). Both behaviours match the docstring.

Indexing by ℕ with value 1 out of range is a junk-value convenience, chosen so that relator words can be written without proofs that the index is in bounds. It does not change the mathematical content, which is the generators of the presented group.

Mathlib has no pro-p presentations, so there is no counterpart. Restricting to `Fin n` is needed by the ℕ-indexing itself. The general case, a presentation on an arbitrary type X with generators `presentedProP.of`, is already in the library, so this definition is not too narrow.
